ai_support::combat_withdrawal::CombatWit.name: CombatWithdrawalFact
ai_support::combat_withdrawal::CombatWit.doc: A conservative fact about removing the currently selected creature from combat.  `None` from [`combat_withdrawal_fact_for_current_target`] means the current prompt is not an exact combat-withdrawal target. `NoCombatPair` means it is one, but the selected object has no one-on-one combat pair to assess.

ai_support::combat_withdrawal::CombatWit.name: CombatWithdrawalTargetRole
ai_support::combat_withdrawal::CombatWit.doc: Whether the selected creature is attacking or blocking in the exact combat pair.

ai_support::context::AiProposalApplicati.name: AiProposalApplication
ai_support::context::AiProposalApplicati.doc: The engine's outcome when it applies an action bound to an issued AI decision contract. Transport adapters use `Stale` to request a fresh decision and surface only `Rejected` as an action failure.

ai_support::evoke::EvokeImmediateOutcome.name: EvokeImmediateOutcome
ai_support::evoke::EvokeImmediateOutcome.doc: What the narrow immediate-Evoke evaluator established.

variants.name: ProvenUseful
variants.doc: Every immediate effect was a recognized beneficial effect with a live, opposing target where one is required.

variants.name: NoBeneficialTarget
variants.doc: Every recognized immediate target effect lacks a beneficial candidate.

variants.name: Unknown
variants.doc: The immediate surface is absent, optional, conditional, modal, mixed, unimplemented, neutral, harmful, or outside this deliberately small set.

ai_support::evoke::EvokePromptDescriptor.name: EvokePromptDescriptor
ai_support::evoke::EvokePromptDescriptor.doc: A live Evoke choice, preserving the engine's prompt representation.

ai_support::filter::FilterCost.name: FilterCost
ai_support::filter::FilterCost.doc: A filter's approximate computational cost. The pipeline runs filters in ascending cost order so the cheapest rejection wins.

variants.name: Trivial
variants.doc: Constant-time structural check (e.g., object-id existence, index bounds).

variants.name: Cheap
variants.doc: Bounded lookup (e.g., iterate known-small lists).

variants.name: Expensive
variants.doc: Requires cloning `GameState` and running `apply_as_current`.

ai_support::payment_continuation::Paymen.name: PaymentContinuationBatchStatus
ai_support::payment_continuation::Paymen.doc: The completedness of one decision-wide payment proof.

variants.name: Complete
variants.doc: Every supplied root was considered within the shared bound. An empty certificate vector is the only proof that no supplied payment finishes.

variants.name: Indeterminate
variants.doc: The search stopped before it could make a no-payment claim. Consumers must not use partial certificates as evidence that payment is available.

ai_support::payment_continuation::Paymen.name: PaymentContinuationIndeterminate
ai_support::payment_continuation::Paymen.doc: Why a batch payment witness could not prove a complete answer.

ai_support::payment_continuation::Paymen.name: PaymentContinuationRoot
ai_support::payment_continuation::Paymen.doc: Mode-free identity of the announced spell or activated ability being paid.  CR 601.2f–i / CR 602.2b: the total cost is locked, paid, and then finalized as the specific announced spell or activated ability. `ConvokeMode` is an immediate-carrier grammar guard, not root identity: several later carriers do not preserve it.

ai_support::payment_continuation::Paymen.name: PaymentContinuationState
ai_support::payment_continuation::Paymen.doc: A payment state classification for AI consumers.

variants.name: NotAffiliated
variants.doc: This is not one of the spell/activation mana-payment carriers owned by this oracle. Existing one-step AI behavior remains authoritative.

variants.name: Affiliated
variants.doc: The state is a supported carrier for this exact payment root.

variants.name: UnsupportedAffiliated
variants.doc: The state advertises an in-flight payment root, but its typed authority cannot prove the root safely. Consumers must fail closed, never fall through to an unrelated first-legal policy.

ai_support::payment_continuation::Paymen.name: PaymentContinuationUnsupported
ai_support::payment_continuation::Paymen.doc: Why an affiliated-looking carrier cannot be witnessed safely.

ai_support::prospective_mana::PactPlanSt.name: PactPlanState
ai_support::prospective_mana::PactPlanSt.doc: The plan deliberately exposes only its lifecycle, never the receipt or a simulated state. A dormant plan stays bound to its exact installed delayed trigger until the engine consumes it or a conflicting state invalidates it.

ai_support::swarm::SwarmWitnessIndetermi.name: SwarmWitnessIndeterminate
ai_support::swarm::SwarmWitnessIndetermi.doc: Why a swarm witness declined to make a combat claim.

ai_support::swarm::SwarmWitnessResult.name: SwarmWitnessResult
ai_support::swarm::SwarmWitnessResult.doc: A complete witness or an explicit conservative abstention.

ai_support::targeted_exchange::TargetedE.name: TargetedExchangeVerdict
ai_support::targeted_exchange::TargetedE.doc: Root-cast tactical result. `Indeterminate` deliberately leaves the root candidate available; the preview is a safety veto, not a second rules engine.

analysis::ability_graph::AbilitySlot.name: AbilitySlot
analysis::ability_graph::AbilitySlot.doc: Which of a source's definitions a node was built from.

variants.name: Ability
variants.doc: `abilities[i]`: the spell ability or an activated ability.

variants.name: Trigger
variants.doc: `triggers[i]`.

variants.name: Replacement
variants.doc: `replacements[i]`.

variants.name: Granted
variants.doc: A grant in `statics[statik].modifications[modification]`.

analysis::ability_graph::AxisKey.name: AxisKey
analysis::ability_graph::AxisKey.doc: The magnitude- and player-id-agnostic projection of [`ResourceAxis`] used **only** for static edge matching. It is a leaf parameterization of the same axis vocabulary (one abstraction level up in genericity, same CR sections), derived from `ResourceAxis` by dropping the runtime payload and adding the axes that have no `ResourceVector` field (`Tap`).  Two round-3 collapses are baked into [`AxisKey::from`]: **R3-MANA-COLLAPSE** — every `Mana(color)` folds to the single color-agnostic [`AxisKey::Mana`] so any mana production intersects any mana cost; and **R3-LANDFALL-COLLAPSE** — both `LandfallTriggers` and `Trigger(Landfall)` fold to [`AxisKey::Landfall`].

variants.name: Mana
variants.doc: CR 106.1: any mana, any color (R3-MANA-COLLAPSE — a single fungible key).

variants.name: Damage
variants.doc: CR 120.1: damage dealt.

variants.name: Life
variants.doc: CR 119.1: life.

variants.name: Library
variants.doc: CR 401: library size.

variants.name: Counter
variants.doc: CR 122.1: a counter of a specific class on a specific object class.

variants.name: AnyCounter
variants.doc: CR 122.1: a **requires-only** wildcard for "remove a counter of any type" costs (R3-COUNTER-FUNGIBILITY); matches any `Counter(_, _)` producer. Never produced by [`AxisKey::from`].

variants.name: Trigger
variants.doc: CR 603: a non-counter trigger/event family (proliferate, magecraft, …).

variants.name: Tokens
variants.doc: CR 111: tokens created.

variants.name: Casts
variants.doc: CR 601: spells cast.

variants.name: Draw
variants.doc: CR 121: cards drawn.

variants.name: Tap
variants.doc: CR 701.26a/b: untapped state — produced by an untap, consumed by a tap. Has no `ResourceVector` numeric axis; injected directly into a node's produces/requires sets.

variants.name: ExtraTurn
variants.doc: CR 500.7: extra turns.

variants.name: Etb
variants.doc: CR 603.6a: enters-the-battlefield triggers.

variants.name: Ltb
variants.doc: CR 603.6c: leaves-the-battlefield triggers.

variants.name: Death
variants.doc: CR 700.4: dies (creature-to-graveyard) triggers.

variants.name: Sac
variants.doc: CR 701.21a: sacrifice triggers.

variants.name: Landfall
variants.doc: CR 603: landfall triggers (R3-LANDFALL-COLLAPSE — the single landfall key).

variants.name: Combat
variants.doc: CR 500.8: extra combat phases.

variants.name: ReturnToHand
variants.doc: CR 608.2n + CR 304.1 + CR 307.1: a card returned from a graveyard to a hand, where a resolved instant or sorcery must be before it can be cast again.

analysis::ability_graph::ModelCompletene.name: ModelCompleteness
analysis::ability_graph::ModelCompletene.doc: Whether every collected `Effect`/cost of a node (or every member node of a candidate) projected to a modeled `ResourceVector`, or at least one folded to [`Projection::Unmodeled`]. A typed candidate-confidence axis replacing a raw `bool` (CLAUDE.md "no raw bool" / R2) — self-documenting and extensible to finer-grained confidence levels without touching call sites.

variants.name: FullyModeled
variants.doc: Every effect/cost projected to a modeled vector.

variants.name: ContainsUnmodeled
variants.doc: ≥1 effect/cost folded to [`Projection::Unmodeled`].

analysis::corpus::DeferralBucket.name: DeferralBucket
analysis::corpus::DeferralBucket.doc: The measured structural reason a non-gated corpus row is not yet driven on today's net-progress loop model. Declarative typed data on every deferred [`ComboRow`] (NOT a per-index `match`), sourced from the "Remaining corpus rows" analysis — see the named-bucket enumerations there. `Other` is the honest catch-all for a deferred row not in one of the three explicitly measured structural classes (no bespoke driver on the current in-place model).

variants.name: ObjectReentry
variants.doc: Tokens / blink / persist / undying / recur engines: every cycle makes a new object. A token mint (CR 111.1) allocates a fresh `ObjectId`; a permanent that leaves the battlefield and returns is a new object (CR 400.7) that the zone mover keeps under its storage `ObjectId` with a new incarnation.

variants.name: ExtraTurnOrCombat
variants.doc: Extra-turn / extra-combat re-entry: each cycle advances `turn_number` / combat count, so the loop point is a different turn/phase — not board- identical.

variants.name: ColorConverting
variants.doc: Color-converting net-progress the per-color rule rejects (a producer that gains one color while a different, unreplaceable color is consumed).

variants.name: Other
variants.doc: Deferred but not among the three explicitly measured structural classes; no bespoke driver on today's in-place loop model.

analysis::corpus::ResourceFamily.name: ResourceFamily
analysis::corpus::ResourceFamily.doc: The §12 unbounded-resource families, mapped to the concrete [`ResourceAxis`] the detector reports. Keeps the corpus table declarative.

variants.name: Confirmed
variants.doc: Driven through the existing detector; cert/family/win_kind match the row.

variants.name: Failed
variants.doc: Driver ran but produced no/mismatched confirmation — a regression.

variants.name: Gated
variants.doc: Card-gated on an unimplemented card (a `gated_on`-nonempty row).

variants.name: Deferred
variants.doc: Testable but no driver yet (measured structural bucket).

analysis::decision_template::AimViolatio.name: AimViolation
analysis::decision_template::AimViolatio.doc: CR 732.2a + CR 102.1: why a declared aim is not a choice this sequence can contain.

variants.name: AimsAtDepartedSeat
variants.doc: At `repetition` the declaration names `seat`, whom the cascade taken under that same declaration removes at `departure` — strictly earlier, so CR 102.1 leaves nobody for the choice to name and CR 732.2a's "may be legally taken" is not met.

analysis::decision_template::Announcemen.name: AnnouncementSubject
analysis::decision_template::Announcemen.doc: CR 115.2 + CR 601.2c: WHO one announcement names, stored in re-bindable form. The storable dual of [`ConcreteTarget`], which already draws exactly this two-way split at the RESOLVED end of the same pipeline — so this adds no categorical boundary, it gives the existing one a pre-resolution spelling.  PROVENANCE, and it is the whole point of the type: a `Seat` here is a TARGET (CR 601.2c), judged by `game::targeting::player_is_legal_target` — existence PLUS CR 702.11c hexproof / CR 702.18a shroud / CR 702.16b protection. A merely CHOSEN player (CR 115.10a — e.g. a CR 701.34a proliferate choice) is NOT this type; it stays [`TargetPin::Player`] and keeps its existence-only authority. Two questions, two spellings.

analysis::decision_template::ChoicePoint.name: ChoicePoint
analysis::decision_template::ChoicePoint.doc: CR 732.2a: WHICH CHOICE a [`DecisionSlot`] names, typed rather than numbered. One variant per choice point a producer constructs a slot for, and the set is closed by [`pin_answers_point`]'s exhaustive, wildcard-free ([`PinnedDecision`] x [`DecisionPointKind`]) product: this enum is that product's point half, so a variant added to either paired enum build-breaks there, where the decision about this enum is then taken explicitly.  The four variants sharing the [`PinnedDecision::Targets`] pin are why the type exists: one object can be a mana ability's cost source AND a resolving trigger's source, so a pin variant plus a source is not an identity.  DECLARATION ORDER IS A DESIGN CONSTRAINT, not an accident: [`DecisionSlot`] derives `Ord` and `GameAction::DeclareShortcut` participates in deterministic AI action ordering, so `AnnouncedTarget` is declared BEFORE `MayGate` to reproduce the order a source's announced-target slot and its "may" slot compared in while the ordinal carried the kind half. That pair is the only one any published set compares; the remaining variants' relative order is free but fixed by this declaration.  `Copy` — which [`DecisionSlot`] itself cannot derive, since [`DecisionSource`] is not `Copy` — so points compare and pass by value.

variants.name: AnnouncedTarget
variants.doc: CR 601.2c (reached for a triggered ability via CR 603.3d) + CR 115.2: a target announced as the spell or ability is put on the stack.

variants.name: MayGate
variants.doc: CR 603.5: the optional "may" a triggered ability's effect offers as it resolves.

variants.name: TriggerOrder
variants.doc: CR 603.3b: the position its controller puts one simultaneously-triggered ability at on the stack.

variants.name: TapCost
variants.doc: CR 602.2b -> CR 601.2h: which permanents the player chose to tap to PAY an activation cost. Activating follows the casting process of CR 601.2b-i, and CR 601.2h is where the total cost is paid.

variants.name: ProliferateSet
variants.doc: CR 701.34a: the permanents and/or players a proliferate chooses — a merely CHOSEN set, not a targeted one.

variants.name: ResolutionSet
variants.doc: CR 608.2d: a set of objects an effect instructs a player to choose as the spell or ability RESOLVES — a choice other than one already made as part of casting.

variants.name: ManaColor
variants.doc: CR 608.2d + CR 605.3b: the color an "add one mana of any color" mana ability produces. CR 605.3b is why that choice never reaches the stack.

variants.name: ConvokeTaps
variants.doc: CR 702.51a: which untapped creatures are tapped to pay convoke.

variants.name: Mode
variants.doc: CR 700.2: which modes of a modal spell or ability were chosen.

variants.name: UnlessBreak
variants.doc: CR 732.6: the pay-or-decline choice an "[A] unless [B]" effect offers inside a loop.

analysis::decision_template::ConcreteDec.name: ConcreteDecision
analysis::decision_template::ConcreteDec.doc: A pin resolved to concrete live values for one iteration.

variants.name: Order
variants.doc: CR 603.3b + CR 400.7: `slot` is the RECORDED identity this decision answers, and it is the whole identity — there is no live binding to carry, because by CR 400.7 the object that asked is not the one standing there at the next repetition.

variants.name: ManaColor
variants.doc: CR 608.2d: the copy-through mana color for this iteration (never fails — no state lookup).

variants.name: ConvokeTaps
variants.doc: CR 601.2h + CR 702.51a/b: the live-resolved convoke tap-set for this iteration — `(creature, mana_type)` pairs to feed as `GameAction::TapForConvoke`. Re-bound each iteration by `select_convoke_taps` in `DetectionFodderFirst` order (CR 702.51a lets the loop replay tap reproduced fodder rather than a stable-partition engine permanent).

analysis::decision_template::DecisionKin.name: DecisionKind
analysis::decision_template::DecisionKin.doc: CR 603.3b (TriggerOrdering) / CR 732.2a (LoopChoice): which decision family a template captures. The `key` discriminant that lets one `decision_templates` Vec hold both the trigger-order templates B2 consults and the loop-choice templates B3/B5 will add, so the gate can filter to `TriggerOrdering` only. The FILTER it enables is load-bearing now (the gate must ignore non-ordering templates), and `LoopChoice`'s own consumer is now known: it is the CROSS-EPISODE CARRIER. A `LoopChoice` entry in `GameState::decision_templates` survives the CR 603.3b batch boundary — `GameState::clear_ephemeral_trigger_order_templates`' retain predicate is scoped to `TriggerOrdering` — so it is the vehicle a later episode's declaration can ride, and it is still POPULATED BY PHASE 4 AND BY NOTHING TODAY. PINNED BY A SHIPPED ROW: `fantastic_four_bounded_loop::r3b_driven_a_loop_choice_carrier_survives_a_whole_ accepted_f4_drive` plants the `(kind × ephemerality)` cells on the real 4-player board and drives a whole accepted CR 732.2a shortcut through `apply()` — the `LoopChoice` cell survives (`3 → 2`) while the `TriggerOrdering` ephemeral cell beside it does not. `loop_shortcut_ranking::r3b_*` is the seam-level statement of the same predicate.

analysis::decision_template::DecisionPoi.name: DecisionPointKind
analysis::decision_template::DecisionPoi.doc: Legal option set for one decision-point. EXHAUSTIVE, wildcard-free 1:1 read-side peer of the loop-declaration [`PinnedDecision`] variants (`Order` is CR 603.3b trigger-ordering, not a loop-declaration choice — it has no read-side peer). Externally tagged → FE-consumable JSON (`{"ConvokeTaps":{"tappable":[..]}}`).

variants.name: Targets
variants.doc: CR 608.2b: the legal targets for the slot (native `find_legal_targets` output).

variants.name: ConvokeTaps
variants.doc: CR 702.51a: untapped creatures the controller may tap for convoke (informational — the concrete taps are re-bound live by `select_convoke_taps`).

variants.name: Mode
variants.doc: CR 700.2 modal: the selectable mode indices.

variants.name: MayChoice
variants.doc: CR 603.5: a binary "may" — the slot alone identifies it (FE renders yes/no).

variants.name: UnlessBreak
variants.doc: CR 732.6: a binary "[A] unless [B]" break — pay or decline.

variants.name: ManaColor
variants.doc: CR 608.2d: a fixed mana-color choice — informational read-side (the color is latched; the FE renders it read-only, there is no per-iteration re-selection). Externally tagged → `{"ManaColor":{"color":"Blue"}}`.

analysis::decision_template::IterationCo.name: IterationCount
analysis::decision_template::IterationCo.doc: CR 732.2a "a loop that repeats a specified number of times". **Phase 1 ships ONLY `Fixed`** (reviewer G7): nothing in Phase 1 reads the count — [`resolve`] takes an explicit `iteration` index, and the count-driven loop that consumes it is Phase 3 / Part A. The count-terminated variants (`UntilLethal` → CR 704.5a "a player with 0 or less life loses"; `UntilResource(ResourceAxis, i64)`) are deferred to the phase that adds their driver, so the shipped surface stays minimal and fully tested. The enum is kept (rather than a bare `u32` field on `Scheduled`) so Phase 3 adds those variants without a field-type change at any `Scheduled` construction site.

variants.name: UntilLethal
variants.doc: CR 704.5a + CR 732.1b: repeat until a player is at 0-or-less life — the driver PR-7 Phase 3 adds for the interactive loop-shortcut of a determinate lethal drain. The terminating condition is the SBA, not a caller-supplied count. (`UntilResource` stays deferred to Phase 4/B5.)

analysis::decision_template::LoopAnswer.name: LoopAnswer
analysis::decision_template::LoopAnswer.doc: The observed answer to ONE published decision slot, from ONE seat, across the current loop-detection window. Journalled under the key `(DecisionSlot, PlayerId)` (`GameState::record_loop_answer`), so a seat can only ever answer for itself and the CHOICE POINT keeps the two slots one source can publish (CR 601.2c target, CR 603.5 "may") in two entries rather than collapsing them into one latched conflict.  CR 732.2a says a shortcut proposal describes "a sequence of game choices, for all players, that may be legally taken based on the current game state and the predictable results of the sequence of choices", and that this sequence "may be a non-repetitive series of choices, a loop that repeats a specified number of times, multiple loops, or nested loops, and may even cross multiple turns". A series whose answers DIFFER between iterations is therefore not, by itself, the conditional action the rule bars; what the rule actually bars is narrower — "It can't include conditional actions, where the outcome of a game event determines the next action a player takes."  This engine refuses on a differing answer anyway. That is an ENGINE-CAPABILITY LIMIT, DELIBERATELY MORE CONSERVATIVE THAN CR 732.2a REQUIRES — not a rule the CR states. [`DecisionTemplate`] pins exactly one `MayChoice` per published slot per cycle, so a non-uniform series has no representation here; it is the same "a choice a player could only make reactively is one they cannot pin" disposition [`predictability_gate`]'s CR 732.2a firewall doc already records. Failing to offer is the fail-closed direction: strictly fewer offers, never a wrong pin.

variants.name: Uniform
variants.doc: Every observed iteration answered this (slot, seat) pair identically.

variants.name: Conflicted
variants.doc: Two observed iterations of the same (slot, seat) pair disagreed. Latched: never returns to `Uniform`. See the type doc — the refusal this produces is this engine's conservative policy, NOT a CR 732.2a mandate.

analysis::decision_template::LoopAnswerV.name: LoopAnswerValue
analysis::decision_template::LoopAnswerV.doc: The VALUE of one observed answer. Variants are distinct CR choice KINDS — the same axis [`PinnedDecision`] and [`DecisionPointKind`] already partition, and under the same CR 732.2a umbrella ("a sequence of game choices, for all players") that makes each of those ONE type rather than one type per rule section. It is therefore a PARTIAL observation-side projection of that kind space (2 of the 6 [`DecisionPointKind`] variants), TOTALIZED at the consumer's wildcard-free `(DecisionPointKind, LoopAnswerValue)` match — not an exhaustive peer of either.  Parameterizing [`LoopAnswer::Uniform`] rather than adding a `UniformTargets` sibling is deliberate: a `X`/`TargetX` sibling pair is CLAUDE.md's sibling-cluster smell, and it would put the KIND axis on the same enum level as the LATCH axis (`Uniform` vs `Conflicted`), which is the layer conflation CLAUDE.md's enum-design rule forbids.  DELIBERATELY DERIVES NO `Serialize`/`Deserialize`, exactly as [`LoopAnswer`] does: the `#[serde(skip)]` on `GameState::loop_answer_journal` is enforced AT COMPILE TIME by the absence of that derive, and adding one here would silently re-open persistence of a transient window. ([`TargetPin`] and [`MayChoiceOption`] do derive it; the bar lives on the two enums above them, which is where it was put.)

variants.name: May
variants.doc: CR 603.5: take the optional action, or decline it.

variants.name: Targets
variants.doc: CR 608.2b + CR 601.2c: the announced targets for one slot, in announcement order.

analysis::decision_template::MayChoiceOp.name: MayChoiceOption
analysis::decision_template::MayChoiceOp.doc: CR 603.5: whether a "may" pin takes the optional action or declines it. Typed (not `bool`) so both outcomes are self-documenting at every construction and match site.

analysis::decision_template::PinValidati.name: PinValidation
analysis::decision_template::PinValidati.doc: CR 732.2a + CR 608.2b: why a declared pin is not a LEGAL answer to the offered decision schema. `validate_pins` is the fail-closed VALUE-legality firewall paired with [`predictability_gate`]'s COVERAGE check: the gate proves every offered slot is pinned; this proves every pin's VALUE lies inside the slot's offered legal set at every index the ACCEPTED COUNT will drive. Any violation ⇒ the declare handler rejects the shortcut and hands back to manual play (no APNAP, no drive, no crown).

variants.name: UnexposedSlot
variants.doc: The pin addresses a slot the offer never exposed (no matching `DecisionPoint`).

variants.name: IllegalPinValue
variants.doc: Raised for two reasons, which no production caller tells apart (see [`declaration_conforms`]'s `bool` return):  * CR 608.2b — a `Targets` pin resolves to a value outside the slot's offered   `legal_targets`, or fails to resolve to a live legal object at all; * CR 732.2c — a `Scheduled` pin declares an announcement no index resolves   ([`schedule_announces_every_declared_subject`]).

variants.name: IllegalModeIndex
variants.doc: CR 700.2: a `Mode` pin names an index outside the slot's `available_modes`.

variants.name: NotALoopDecision
variants.doc: CR 603.3b + CR 732.2a: the pin is a trigger-ordering choice, which is not one of the per-iteration choices a loop declaration answers. It addresses no slot, so it carries the source rather than a [`DecisionSlot`].

variants.name: DivergesFromRecordedPeriod
variants.doc: CR 732.2a: the pin answers its slot otherwise than the confirmed period did, so it declares a sequence nobody confirmed.

analysis::decision_template::PinnedDecis.name: PinnedDecision
analysis::decision_template::PinnedDecis.doc: One pinned decision. Variants are distinct CR choice KINDS (ordering / targeting / modal / optional-"may" / "[A] unless [B]" break), not a parameterization axis.

variants.name: Order
variants.doc: CR 603.3b: place this slot's trigger at ordering position `pos`. Its slot is minted at [`ChoicePoint::TriggerOrder`] and nowhere else, which is what keeps an ordering pin outside a declaration's slot space: no PUBLISHED point carries `TriggerOrder`.

variants.name: Targets
variants.doc: CR 608.2b: targets for a slot; each re-resolved to a live legal ObjectId per iteration.

variants.name: Mode
variants.doc: CR 700.2 modal: chosen mode indices (mirrors `GameAction::SelectModes.indices`).

variants.name: MayChoice
variants.doc: CR 603.5 / a "may" effect: take the optional action or not.

variants.name: UnlessBreak
variants.doc: CR 732.6: pay or decline an "[A] unless [B]" break.

variants.name: ConvokeTaps
variants.doc: CR 601.2h + CR 702.51a/b: pay a convoke `ManaPayment` by tapping the minimal deterministic set of untapped creatures matching the live post-affinity color requirement. State-independent: the concrete creatures are re-bound LIVE each iteration (fodder-first order — reproduced tokens preferred, then lowest ObjectId within each class) via `select_convoke_taps`, a pure function of (live legal untapped set, locked cost) per CR 732.2a — so no per-iteration creature is latched here.

variants.name: ManaColor
variants.doc: CR 608.2d + CR 605.3b: a fixed mana-color choice for an "add one mana of any color" mana ability whose product pays a colored downstream cost (the loop's mana-neutrality authority — e.g. Relic of Legends' Blue feeding Freed from the Real's `{U}` untap). LATCHED to the color the player produced in the demonstrated iteration and copied through unchanged every replay (the color is a constant, not a per-iteration re-binding — CR 732.2a "predictable results"). Distinct CR choice KIND (color selection, CR 608.2d), not a parameterization of the target/modal/may axes. `slot.point` disambiguates it from a tap-cost `Targets` pin on the SAME mana-ability source — [`ChoicePoint::ManaColor`] against [`ChoicePoint::TapCost`], a type fact rather than a numbering convention.

variants.name: UnpinnedChoice
variants.doc: CR 732.2a: a cycle choice slot has no matching `PinnedDecision` ⇒ not a describable predictable sequence ⇒ no auto-resolve.

analysis::decision_template::RankingErro.name: RankingError
analysis::decision_template::RankingErro.doc: Why a subject list is not a legal [`Ranking`]. Both clauses are refused at CONSTRUCTION, which is what makes [`Ranking::head`] infallible — no `Option` leaks into the resolver, and a wire-supplied list fails the LOAD rather than the drive (the same disposition `reject_zero_bound_shortcut_offer` takes for a wire-sourced `deliverable_capacity`).

variants.name: Empty
variants.doc: An empty ranking names nobody: there is no head to announce.

variants.name: DuplicateSubject
variants.doc: CR 601.2c: an announcement names its choice per target. A repeated subject is not an ordering — it is the same declaration twice, and it would make the tail unreachable.

analysis::decision_template::ReplayFailu.name: ReplayFailure
analysis::decision_template::ReplayFailu.doc: Why a replay could not produce a legal concrete decision this iteration. **Selection is by PIN KIND, never by `ReplayMode`** (reviewer G2): a `Static`-mode template can carry `Targets` pins (an ordered AND targeted trigger), so the failure kind is chosen by which pin/target is being resolved, independent of whether the template is `Static` or `Scheduled`.

variants.name: IllegalTarget
variants.doc: CR 608.2b: a TARGET pin no longer resolves to a legal live target (left its zone / ceased to exist / CR 800.4 + CR 102.1 left the game). Raised whenever a *target* is illegal-or-absent, in ANY `ReplayMode`. ⇒ abort the auto-shortcut, hand back to manual.  Carries the [`TargetPin`] itself rather than a `DecisionSource`: `Player` and `Scheduled` pins are equally capable of going illegal, and a `DecisionSource` can name neither. Parameterizing the existing variant keeps ONE "target went illegal" failure instead of growing a per-pin-kind sibling cluster.

variants.name: ScheduleExhausted
variants.doc: A `RoundRobin`/`Piecewise` schedule has no entry covering this iteration index.

variants.name: UnpayableConvoke
variants.doc: CR 702.51b: no legal untapped-creature tap-set covers the live convoke requirement (the post-affinity locked cost can't be paid by the available untapped creatures + pool) ⇒ abort the auto-shortcut, hand back to manual.

analysis::decision_template::ReplayMode.name: ReplayMode
analysis::decision_template::ReplayMode.doc: CR 732.2a: how the pins are replayed. `Static` (ordering) ignores the iteration index; `Scheduled` (loop shortcut) makes every choice a pure function of it.

analysis::decision_template::TargetPin.name: TargetPin
analysis::decision_template::TargetPin.doc: A pinned target. `ByIdentity` re-resolves to a live legal ObjectId each iteration (CR 608.2b); `Scheduled` is an iteration-indexed pure function (CR 732.2a).

variants.name: Player
variants.doc: A CONSTANT **CHOICE-class** seat (CR 115.10a): this pin answers EVERY firing of its source within the period with the declared player. A seat is state-independent by construction — it can never denote "the newest copy" — so no iteration can turn the pin into the conditional action CR 732.2a forbids.  # THE TWO CLASSES NOW HAVE TWO SPELLINGS, AND THIS ONE IS THE CHOICE CLASS  CR 115.10a: "unless that object or player is identified by the word 'target' … it's not a target". A seat this pin names was CHOSEN, not targeted, so [`resolve_target`] judges it by `game::players::player_exists_for_choice` — EXISTENCE ONLY. Applying the targeting-only exclusions (CR 702.11c hexproof / CR 702.18a shroud / CR 702.16b protection) here would refuse legal CR 732.2a proposals; that over-veto is what `game::engine`'s `a_shrouded_player_pin_is_still_published_by_the_offer_builder` and `a_shrouded_seat_is_untargetable_yet_still_choosable_at_the_pin_recheck` (this module) exist to keep out. Its live in-process producer is the CR 701.34a proliferate choice (`game::engine::proliferate_pins`).  A CR 601.2c **TARGET**-class seat is a different question and takes the other spelling: [`AnnouncementSubject::Seat`] inside a [`Ranking`] inside [`TargetPin::Scheduled`], judged by `game::targeting::player_is_legal_target`. Both TARGET-class producers emit that spelling — `game::engine::record_trigger_target_answer` (the engine's own CR 601.2c announcement journal) and `game::interaction::materialize_loop_shortcut_response` (the human ingress of the same point kind). The spelling IS the provenance, so the authority is selected by what the answer IS, never by who submitted it.

analysis::decision_template::TargetSched.name: TargetSchedule
analysis::decision_template::TargetSched.doc: CR 732.2a "predictable results / no conditional actions": deterministic, iteration-indexed target variation. EVERY variant is a pure function of (iteration index, live legal set) — NEVER of a prior iteration's OUTCOME. That is enforced BY CONSTRUCTION: no variant carries any prior-outcome/event input, so a "react to what happened" target is unrepresentable (this is what collapses the predictability gate's "no conditional" clause into "total coverage").  AND THE PURITY INVARIANT IS NARROWER THAN "consults the live set", now that each step carries a [`Ranking`] rather than a single subject: a variant consults the live legal set to **re-bind the declared subject** (CR 400.7); it never uses the live set to **substitute a different subject**. Selecting a different entry because a game event removed the first is exactly the conditional action CR 732.2a bars — which is why `evaluate_schedule` reads a step's [`Ranking::head`] and nothing else.

variants.name: Piecewise
variants.doc: Pre-declared switch-over: identity for [start, next-start). The switch point is FIXED IN ADVANCE (not triggered by an in-loop event), keeping it 732.2a-predictable.

analysis::decision_template::UnlessPayme.name: UnlessPaymentOption
analysis::decision_template::UnlessPayme.doc: CR 732.6: whether an "[A] unless [B]" pin pays [B] to break the loop, or declines and takes [A].

analysis::loop_check::OfferRoad.name: OfferRoad
analysis::loop_check::OfferRoad.doc: Which producer minted a loop-shortcut offer: the ring sampler, or the priority holder's recorded period.

analysis::loop_check::ShortcutResponse.name: ShortcutResponse
analysis::loop_check::ShortcutResponse.doc: CR 732.2b/c: an opponent's answer to a proposed loop shortcut. `Accept` lets the shortcut proceed; `Shorten` names an earlier stopping point.  CR 732.2b lets a shortening player name the PLACE now and the choice later — "the player doesn't need to specify at this time what the new choice will be" — which is why `Shorten` carries `at_iteration` and no choice payload.  `at_iteration` is a partial-advance instruction, not a stop signal: the named place becomes the proposal's count, the poll runs on to the last player, and the shortcut is then taken to that place (CR 732.2c). `ShortcutProposal::shortened_by` carries whose place it is.

variants.name: Accept
variants.doc: CR 732.2c: this player agrees to take the shortcut.

variants.name: Shorten
variants.doc: CR 732.2b: this player names an earlier ending point (`at_iteration` cycles in).

analysis::loop_check::WinKind.name: WinKind
analysis::loop_check::WinKind.doc: How a confirmed net-progress loop reaches a win (or merely accrues unbounded advantage), derived from its unbounded resource axes.  This is the engine-side, analysis-owned classification. It deliberately does **not** reuse `phase-ai`'s `combo::WinKind` — that enum lives in a crate that *depends on* `engine`, so it cannot be imported here, and it is a coarser 3-variant author's-claim vocabulary (`ImmediateLoss` / `InfiniteLoop` / `LethalDamage`). The detector classifies the *measured* unbounded axis, so it needs the finer set below; PR-8 maps this onto `combo::WinKind` when it couples the certificate into the AI.  PR-7 Phase 3: gains `Serialize`/`Deserialize` because it now rides inside `WaitingFor::LoopShortcut`'s `LoopCertificate` and `ShortcutProposal` across the serialization boundary (all fields are derived from public board state — no hidden info). Serde default (externally tagged): each unit variant serializes as its bare name string.

variants.name: LethalDamage
variants.doc: CR 704.5a: an opponent's life is driven to 0 or less — unbounded damage to or unbounded life loss from an opponent (burn pings, drains, lifeloss).

variants.name: PoisonLoss
variants.doc: CR 704.5c: an opponent accrues 10+ poison counters — an unbounded poison (infect/proliferate-poison) loop.

variants.name: Decking
variants.doc: CR 104.3c / CR 121.4: an opponent's library is emptied (mill) such that the next draw — or the mill itself reaching 0 — loses them the game. Surfaces as an unbounded *downward* library axis on an opponent.

variants.name: ImmediateWin
variants.doc: CR 104.2: an explicit "you win the game" / "that player loses the game" effect fires each cycle (e.g. an Aetherflux-style life-payment, a Thassa's-Oracle-style deckout win). Reserved for loops whose win is a printed win/loss condition rather than a resource threshold.

variants.name: ExtraTurns
variants.doc: CR 500.7: unbounded extra turns — a turns loop that wins by simply never passing the game back.

variants.name: Advantage
variants.doc: A loop that accrues an unbounded *advantage* resource (mana, tokens, cards drawn, casts, combat phases, generic triggers, +1/+1 or loyalty counters, death/ETB/LTB/sac trigger engines) without, by itself, being a direct loss condition for an opponent. The canonical CR 732.2a beneficial loop; the payoff that converts the advantage to a win is a separate card.

analysis::resource::AnnouncedLead.name: AnnouncedLead
analysis::resource::AnnouncedLead.doc: CR 601.2c + CR 603.3d: which charged slots' first repetition resolves a target announced before the shortcut was proposed. A triggered ability's targets are chosen as it is put on the stack, so a charged slot whose trigger already sits on the stack of the board a drive starts from resolves the aim the offer published at the drive's first repetition, and the declaration under test governs that slot from the second. A charged slot with no announcement on that stack is announced inside the drive and resolves the declaration under test from the first repetition. Which slots lead is a fact of that board, slot by slot, and never of the loop.  Stated by the caller rather than read off `state`: the declare seam and the consumption seam hand the walk the same pre-drive board and ask it different questions. Not a bound direction — that axis is [`ChargeBound`]'s.

variants.name: None
variants.doc: No charged slot leads: every repetition resolves the declaration under test at its own index.

variants.name: LeadingRepetition
variants.doc: The listed charged slots lead by one repetition: each resolves the declaration the offer published at the first repetition, and the declaration under test from the second, at its index less one. A charged slot not listed leads by nothing.

analysis::resource::ChargeBound.name: ChargeBound
analysis::resource::ChargeBound.doc: CR 732.2a: which direction a charge stream's error is required to land in. The model is asked two questions whose safe failures are opposite, so the direction is a parameter of the one producer rather than a property of it.

variants.name: Ceiling
variants.doc: The most a conforming declaration can take from the seat. An over-charge lowers a count, which is the direction a published ceiling and a drivability gate must fail in.

variants.name: Attributable
variants.doc: What THIS declaration's own aims take: an aim the observation made and this declaration does not is SUBTRACTED rather than held fail-closed, and an unresolved term falls to the admitting side, because CR 704.3's live sweep and the drive's own two conformance authorities catch a wrongly admitted declaration while nothing catches a wrongly refused one.

analysis::resource::CounterClass.name: CounterClass
analysis::resource::CounterClass.doc: CR 122.1: analysis-layer classification of a counter kind.  The engine's [`CounterType`] is intentionally **not** reused as a map key here: it derives neither `Ord` (required for `BTreeMap` keys) nor a small closed set — it carries `Generic(String)`, `Keyword(KeywordKind)`, and parameterized `PowerToughness { .. }` variants. Adding `Ord` to that crate-wide enum (and transitively to `KeywordKind`) to satisfy one analysis map would be a far larger, non-additive change. Instead this module owns a small `Ord` classification of the counter dimensions the corpus cares about (CR 122.1: +1/+1, loyalty, poison, …) and folds the long tail into `Other`.

variants.name: Plus1Plus1
variants.doc: CR 122.1a: a +1/+1 counter.

variants.name: Minus1Minus1
variants.doc: CR 122.1a: a -1/-1 counter.

variants.name: Loyalty
variants.doc: CR 306.5b: a loyalty counter on a planeswalker.

variants.name: Defense
variants.doc: CR 310.4c: a defense counter on a battle.

variants.name: Poison
variants.doc: CR 122.1 + CR 704.5c: a poison counter on a player (10 ⇒ that player loses).

variants.name: Energy
variants.doc: CR 122.1: an energy counter ({E}) in a player's energy reserve.

variants.name: Other
variants.doc: Any other counter kind (charge, lore, time, keyword, generic, …).

analysis::resource::CoveredGrowth.name: CoveredGrowth
analysis::resource::CoveredGrowth.doc: CR 732.1b: whether a mint of bare tapped copies under the period's controller makes what a cover admitted as the period's growth.

variants.name: Mintable
variants.doc: Objects of the grown class and nothing else, each under the period's controller.

variants.name: PerformedOnly
variants.doc: CR 702.10b + CR 603.7a + CR 111.2 + CR 701.17b: a grown object carries a keyword, a delayed trigger acts on it alone, another player controls it, or a certified instructed departure moved it, so only performing the period makes it.

analysis::resource::FodderCoverRefusal.name: FodderCoverRefusal
analysis::resource::FodderCoverRefusal.doc: A condition of [`loop_states_cover_modulo_fodder_growth`] that refused a frame pair, in the order the cover evaluates them.

analysis::resource::ObjectClass.name: ObjectClass
analysis::resource::ObjectClass.doc: CR 122.1: classification of the object/player a counter sits on, so a counter axis is keyed by *what kind of thing accumulates it* (a +1/+1 loop on a creature is a different unbounded resource than loyalty on a planeswalker).  Typed rather than stringly so the win-classifier can `match` exhaustively.

variants.name: Creature
variants.doc: CR 302: a creature on the battlefield.

variants.name: Planeswalker
variants.doc: CR 306: a planeswalker on the battlefield.

variants.name: Battle
variants.doc: CR 310: a battle on the battlefield.

variants.name: Player
variants.doc: CR 119 / CR 122: a player (poison, energy, experience, …).

variants.name: Other
variants.doc: Any other counter-bearing object (artifact, enchantment, land, …).

analysis::resource::ObjectGrowthVerdict.name: ObjectGrowthVerdict
analysis::resource::ObjectGrowthVerdict.doc: CR 732.2a: the object-growth producer's verdict on its three settle frames, by the recurrence arm that answered.

variants.name: FodderGrowth
variants.doc: One homogeneous class was minted: each frame pair's fodder-cover refusals.

variants.name: ResourceRecurrence
variants.doc: Nothing was minted: the latest arm of the no-mint cover either pair needed, or `None` when a pair does not recur.

analysis::resource::PeriodCertification.name: PeriodCertification
analysis::resource::PeriodCertification.doc: CR 732.2a: WHICH certificate a window's touch is derived under.  The frozen exemption's extrapolation limb needs BOTH a board-level premise that the certified period cannot SHRINK the stack (P2) AND the Karp–Miller read-surface guard that makes the fast-forward the repetition of the observed period (P4). Exactly one certifying disjunct supplies both, so the exemption is keyed to the DISJUNCT rather than to the basis — as a type rather than a call-site convention, which an executor can drop.  Two of the three variants behave identically today, deliberately: collapsing the equality disjunct onto [`PeriodCertification::ResourceSignatureOnly`] would make the type lie about provenance (equality DOES consult a board predicate), and a mislabel is the fail-open re-entry path. `pub` for ONE reason: it is the type of [`crate::game::engine::MintMeter`]'s `certification` field, the only surface on which the certifying disjunct is observable at all. Do not widen it further.

variants.name: BoardCovered
variants.doc: Basis A, COVER disjunct — the pair passed [`loop_states_cover_modulo_growth_pinned`]. P2: item (2)'s `stack_covers` ⇒ strictly growing depth. P4: items (4)/(5) ⇒ no current-stack entry and no live fire-time condition reads a still-projected axis. This is the ONLY value under which `frozen_ids` is non-empty.

variants.name: BoardEqualOnly
variants.doc: Basis A, EQUALITY disjunct — the pair passed [`loop_states_equal_modulo_resources`]. P2 holds (the stack is compared exactly ⇒ constant depth) but P4 does NOT: that predicate has no items (4)/(5), as its own inherited-assumption section says. A replacement that arms mid-extrapolation is exactly the route P4 forecloses, so `frozen_ids` is forced EMPTY here.

variants.name: ResourceSignatureOnly
variants.doc: Basis B — [`ring_delta_signature`] only, which by its own doc "does not consult a board predicate". Neither P2 nor P4 ⇒ `frozen_ids` is forced EMPTY and the resolution gate scans every current-stack entry.

analysis::resource::RecurrenceCover.name: RecurrenceCover
analysis::resource::RecurrenceCover.doc: CR 732.2a: which arm of the no-mint cover certified a frame pair.

variants.name: Equal
variants.doc: Equal modulo projected resources.

variants.name: CounterGrowth
variants.doc: Covered modulo preserved-`Generic` counter growth.

variants.name: Departure
variants.doc: Covered once a certified instructed departure is stripped.

variants.name: History
variants.doc: Covered once per-turn and per-game history no live surface reads is equalized.

variants.name: TurnCycle
variants.doc: Covered once the caster's own turns and their draws are equalized.

analysis::resource::ResourceAxis.name: ResourceAxis
analysis::resource::ResourceAxis.doc: A tagged, named resource axis — the typed identity of one unbounded resource, used by the `WinKind` classifier to describe a loop certificate.

variants.name: Poison
variants.doc: CR 704.5c: poison counters on a player (10 ⇒ that player loses). Appended at the END to keep the derived `Ord` discriminant of every earlier variant stable.

analysis::resource::TriggerKind.name: TriggerKind
analysis::resource::TriggerKind.doc: A non-counter, non-mana trigger/event family whose firings a loop can pump without changing the board (the canonical example is proliferate, but also magecraft, constellation, etc.). Typed rather than stringly.  CR 701.x keyword-action and CR 603.x triggered-ability families. These counts are **not** directly readable from a `GameState` snapshot — they are events, not stored totals — so [`ResourceVector::snapshot`] always leaves [`ResourceVector::generic_triggers`] empty and the simulation harness feeds them.

variants.name: Proliferate
variants.doc: CR 701.34: proliferate (the keyword action a loop can pump mana-neutrally).

variants.name: Magecraft
variants.doc: CR 207.2c + CR 603: magecraft — an ability word (no individual CR entry) for a triggered ability that fires on casting/copying an instant or sorcery.

variants.name: Constellation
variants.doc: CR 207.2c + CR 603: constellation — an ability word for a triggered ability that fires when an enchantment enters under your control.

variants.name: Landfall
variants.doc: CR 207.2c + CR 603: landfall — an ability word for a triggered ability that fires when a land enters under your control.

variants.name: Other
variants.doc: Any other tracked trigger/keyword-action family.

database::legality::CedhBracketError.name: CedhBracketError
database::legality::CedhBracketError.doc: Error returned when one or more decks in a cEDH table are not declared as `CommanderBracketTier::Cedh`.  cEDH is a manual-declaration-only tier: the bracket estimator never returns `Cedh` algorithmically (see `bracket_estimate.rs:18-27` and the `estimator_never_returns_cedh` test). Validation is therefore a simple tag check — every deck at a cEDH table must carry the explicit declaration.  Kept as an enum (rather than a struct) to accommodate anticipated future variants once Phase 8 wires this validation into the game-init boundary — e.g., `AllDecksUnconfigured` (table has no bracket declarations at all) or `TableSizeMismatch` (seat count doesn't match expected player count).

variants.name: DeckNotCedh
variants.doc: The deck at `seat_index` was not declared as `Cedh`.

variants.name: TooManyPlayers
variants.doc: The proposed table has more than 4 seats. cEDH is exclusively played at 4-player free-for-all tables; the difficulty preset's search budgets are calibrated for that count, and the 5-6+ player scaling path (`create_config_for_players`) silently clips them in a way that breaks the preset's combat-lookahead + paranoid-skip contract. Reject explicitly at setup so users see a clear error instead of an AI that silently underperforms.

database::synthesis::CommanderQualificat.name: CommanderQualification
database::synthesis::CommanderQualificat.doc: CR 903.3 / CR 702.124k: how a card qualifies to be designated a commander.  This is the decomposition of [`type_line_commander_eligible`], not a sibling of it: the general predicate is *defined in terms of* this one, so every existing caller of the general predicate is unaffected. The distinction exists because CR 903.13f(3) grants the partner ability only to a card that "can be a player's commander **by itself**" — a condition no predicate in the tree previously drew.

variants.name: ByItself
variants.doc: CR 903.3 (a)–(c) + CR 903.3a: designatable as the sole commander.

variants.name: OnlyAlongsideChooseABackground
variants.doc: CR 702.124k: a legendary Background enchantment card, which "can't be your commander unless you have also designated a commander with 'choose a Background'".

variants.name: No
variants.doc: Not commander-eligible by type line.

database::synthesis::LayoutKind.name: LayoutKind
database::synthesis::LayoutKind.doc: Internal layout classification from MTGJSON layout strings.

variants.name: Prepare
variants.doc: CR 702.xxx: Prepare (Strixhaven) — Adventure-family two-face layout. Assign when WotC publishes SOS CR update.

variants.name: Specialize
variants.doc: Digital-only Specialize (Alchemy Horizons: Baldur's Gate).

game::ability_utils::WalkOp.name: WalkOp
game::ability_utils::WalkOp.doc: The five units of work in the target-completion walk. The walk charges each one to its [`WorkBudget`] immediately before performing it, and performs it only when that charge succeeded.

variants.name: RecursiveEntry
variants.doc: Entering one walk frame: the root call and every recursion.

variants.name: OptionalSkip
variants.doc: Taking an optional slot's skip branch (CR 115.6).

variants.name: CandidateGeneration
variants.doc: Computing one slot's legal candidates.

variants.name: PrefixValidation
variants.doc: Validating a partial assignment extended by one candidate.

variants.name: LeafValidation
variants.doc: Validating a complete assignment before offering it to the visitor.

game::ability_utils::WalkOutcome.name: WalkOutcome
game::ability_utils::WalkOutcome.doc: The result of one target-completion walk.

variants.name: Accepted
variants.doc: The visitor accepted a legal completion.

variants.name: Rejected
variants.doc: The walk finished: the visitor accepted no legal completion.

variants.name: BudgetExhausted
variants.doc: The budget ran out first, so the walk answers neither way.

game::bracket_estimate::CommanderBracket.name: CommanderBracketTier
game::bracket_estimate::CommanderBracket.doc: Commander bracket tier. The estimator returns only `Core`–`Optimized` (B2–B4). `Exhibition` and `Cedh` are manual self-declarations kept on the frontend's existing manual picker — the estimator never returns them.

game::card_subset::AiCardSubsetResult.name: AiCardSubsetResult
game::card_subset::AiCardSubsetResult.doc: Result of building an AI-worker card subset for one game. `Full` means the caller must load the full database instead (the universe is unbounded).

game::card_subset::FullDbReason.name: FullDbReason
game::card_subset::FullDbReason.doc: Why a game cannot use a bounded AI card subset and must ship the full DB. Open enum: add a variant + one `game_requires_full_card_db` arm for any future whole-corpus mechanic. Never special-case a card.

variants.name: Momir
variants.doc: CR 707.2 + CR 202.3: the Momir emblem creates a token that's a copy (CR 707.2) of a random creature card with the chosen mana value (CR 202.3), drawn at RESOLUTION time from the whole creature corpus via `GameState::card_db` (`create_token_copy_from_pool`). The candidate set is therefore whatever database the resolving engine has loaded: a subset DB silently narrows it to the handful of cards this game's decks reference, so Momir games must give AI workers the full DB.

variants.name: BoosterPack
variants.doc: CR 400.11 + CR 400.11b: `Effect::OpenBoosterPack` stocks its shelf from the ENTIRE printed corpus at rehydrate (`game::boosters::build_shelf`), because a pack may contain any card from any set. A subset DB carries only this game's cards, so no set could fill a pack and the shelf would come back empty — an AI worker would then simulate every booster open as doing nothing. Games that can open a pack use the full DB.

game::casting::ActivationCostGuardSite.name: ActivationCostGuardSite
game::casting::ActivationCostGuardSite.doc: The activation cost-work entries that refuse an unlocked cost. Each is a function that can begin paying part of an activation's cost.

variants.name: DirectPay
variants.doc: `activate_with_cost_carrier`'s untargeted direct payment.

variants.name: ReturnAfterAutomatic
variants.doc: `finish_selected_return_to_hand_after_automatic`.

variants.name: ReturnToHand
variants.doc: `handle_return_to_hand_for_cost`.

variants.name: RemoveCounter
variants.doc: `handle_remove_counter_for_cost`.

variants.name: RemoveCounterDistribution
variants.doc: `handle_remove_counter_distribution_for_cost`.

variants.name: PushToStack
variants.doc: `push_activated_ability_to_stack`, at its entry.

variants.name: ManaResume
variants.doc: `finalize_mana_payment_with_resume`'s activation branch.

variants.name: PhyrexianResume
variants.doc: `finalize_mana_payment_with_phyrexian_choices`'s activation branch.

game::casting::ActivationQuery.name: ActivationQuery
game::casting::ActivationQuery.doc: CR 602.5 + CR 118.3: what the activation gate was asked to decide.  The gate has one body and two consumers. `Legality` is enforcement: it short-circuits at the CR 118.3 affordability exit, which is the cheapest correct answer for "may this be activated". `BlockReason` is the display read-out: it records the affordability verdict and CONTINUES into the target-legality tail, because "you can't pay for this" is only a truthful explanation once everything else about the activation is known to be legal. `BlockReason` is therefore strictly MORE work than `Legality`, which is why it lives behind a separate entry point (`ai_support::activation_block_reasons`) rather than a widened `legal_actions_full`.  **`Legal` is not authoritative under `BlockReason`.** That mode additionally declines the display carve-outs (costless / tap-only costs, and refusals that are structural rather than resource-based) by returning `Illegal` before the payability probe runs, so an affordable tap-only ability reports `Illegal` there. Only `CostNotPayableNow` carries meaning in that mode. Every enforcement caller must use `Legality`.

variants.name: Legality
variants.doc: Enforcement: may this player activate this ability right now?

variants.name: BlockReason
variants.doc: Display: is this ability being withheld SOLELY because the cost is unpayable right now?

game::casting::ActivationVerdict.name: ActivationVerdict
game::casting::ActivationVerdict.doc: CR 602.5 + CR 118.3: the activation gate's verdict.  `CostNotPayableNow` means every other activation requirement passed — the CR 602.5 prohibition statics, the activation zone (CR 602.1), the timing restrictions, CR 302.6 summoning sickness, the modal-mode count and target legality (CR 601.2c) — and only the CR 118.3 resource gate refused. Anything else that refuses yields `Illegal`, so a missing target can never be reported as a payment problem.

variants.name: Legal
variants.doc: The ability may be activated right now.

variants.name: Illegal
variants.doc: The ability may not be activated, for a reason that is not a CR 118.3 resource shortfall (or for a shortfall under `ActivationQuery::Legality`, which does not distinguish).

variants.name: CostNotPayableNow
variants.doc: CR 118.3: legal in every other respect; the player cannot pay the post-reduction activation cost right now.

game::casting::StructurallySelectableAlt.name: StructurallySelectableAlternateSpellPayload
game::casting::StructurallySelectableAlt.doc: CR 601.2b: A player chooses an alternative casting method while casting, before mutable cost and condition checks determine whether it is payable.  An independently stored spell-definition payload that the current casting routes can select before cast-time affordability and other mutable checks.  These are deliberately definition payloads rather than prepared variants: a consumer deciding whether a prospective cast can change a later payoff must not discard a route merely because its cost or condition is false now.

variants.name: BackFace
variants.doc: CR 715.3a + CR 720.3a + CR 712.8c: Adventure and Omen casts evaluate their alternative characteristics, while transformed or converted double-faced casts use their back-face characteristics.  An Adventure/Omen, More Than Meets the Eye, or Disturb route swaps to the stored face before the spell is prepared.

variants.name: FuseRightSpellAbility
variants.doc: CR 702.102a: Fuse lets a player cast both halves of a split card from their hand, appending the right-half spell instructions.

variants.name: Cleave
variants.doc: CR 702.148a: Cleave replaces the card's normal spell text with its bracketless alternate definition while casting it.  Cleave replaces all four stored definition classes before preparation.

game::combat::AttackTarget.name: AttackTarget
game::combat::AttackTarget.doc: Represents who a creature is attacking: a player, planeswalker, or battle (CR 506.3).

game::combat::CombatRequirement.name: CombatRequirement
game::combat::CombatRequirement.doc: Display-only combat legality constraint surfaced on the declare-attackers / declare-blockers waiting payloads so the frontend can render on-card badges and gate the Confirm action WITHOUT recomputing any rules. The engine is the single authority: each entry is derived from the same predicates that enforce legality in `validate_attackers` / `validate_blockers_for_player`. Mirrors the existing `block_requirements` (menace) precedent.

variants.name: MustAttack
variants.doc: CR 508.1d + CR 701.15b: this creature attacks this combat if able. `defenders` carries the CR 508.1d specific-defender requirements (`StaticMode::MustAttackDefender`) intersected with the currently attackable defenders — players, planeswalkers, and battles alike per CR 506.3, so a Gideon Jura lure surfaces exactly like a player lure. Empty for a generic "attacks each combat if able" requirement or for goad with no surviving specific-defender constraint. `sources` names the objects imposing the requirement (intrinsic → the creature itself; remote → the anthem/`Goaded`-static carrier). EMPTY when the only cause is player-level goad (`goaded_by`), which carries no object (CR 701.15b).  `serde`: pre-widening snapshots wrote this field as `players`, holding bare `PlayerId` integers. Both the NAME and the ELEMENT SHAPE therefore need a compat path — the `alias` covers the name, and [`deserialize_defenders`] widens each legacy integer to `AttackTarget::Player`. The two element shapes are disjoint (number vs. tagged map), so the widening is unambiguous. Mirrors the identical legacy-integer shims on [`RequiredDefender`] and `ObjectIncarnationRef`.

variants.name: MustBlock
variants.doc: CR 509.1c: this creature blocks this combat if able. `sources` = the `MustBlock` static carriers.

variants.name: CantAttack
variants.doc: CR 508.1c: this creature can't attack (informational — the UI greys it). `sources` = the restriction carriers (Pacifism, Angelic Arbiter).

variants.name: CantBlock
variants.doc: CR 509.1b: this creature can't block (informational — the UI greys it). `sources` = the "can't block" restriction carriers.

game::combat::CombatTaxPosture.name: CombatTaxPosture
game::combat::CombatTaxPosture.doc: CR 508.1d + CR 509.1c: how a proposal's author treats a combat-tax quote.  Declaring a combat tax is the paying player's choice, so a proposal cannot be completed without knowing whether its author intends to pay. Under `Refuse` any taxed proposal collapses to the deterministic tax-free witness, so no `CombatTaxPayment` prompt is ever opened. `Accept` keeps a taxed proposal intact, but only while the paying player can actually cover the quote, so a completed declaration never opens a prompt whose price its author cannot meet.

variants.name: Refuse
variants.doc: Drop taxed creatures rather than open a tax prompt.

variants.name: Accept
variants.doc: Keep taxed creatures and pay the quote.

game::combat::MaximumBlockDeclarationBlo.name: MaximumBlockDeclarationBlockability
game::combat::MaximumBlockDeclarationBlo.doc: Bounded answer for an AI-only existential block-declaration query.

game::combat::TrampleKind.name: TrampleKind
game::combat::TrampleKind.doc: CR 702.19: Which trample variant applies to combat damage assignment.

variants.name: Standard
variants.doc: CR 702.19b: Standard trample — excess to attack target.

variants.name: OverPlaneswalkers
variants.doc: CR 702.19c: Trample over planeswalkers — excess can spill to PW controller.

game::combat_damage::CombatImpact.name: CombatImpact
game::combat_damage::CombatImpact.doc: Conservative assessment of a bound attacker/blocker pair's next combat-damage exchange.

variants.name: Paid
variants.doc: The cost was paid in full.

variants.name: Paused
variants.doc: CR 614.6 + CR 616.1: replacement processing interrupted payment, either for replacement ordering or for an interactive substitute.

variants.name: Failed
variants.doc: CR 601.2h / CR 118.12: the cost was not (fully) paid. The caller maps this to the scope-appropriate failure channel (see [`PaymentScope`]).

game::coverage::GapDiagnosis.name: GapDiagnosis
game::coverage::GapDiagnosis.doc: Why a coverage gap exists, typed by layer: a parser verdict or an unhandled resolver feature.

game::coverage::ParseCategory.name: ParseCategory
game::coverage::ParseCategory.doc: The category of a parsed item in the coverage tree.

game::coverage::ResolverFeatureFamily.name: ResolverFeatureFamily
game::coverage::ResolverFeatureFamily.doc: A resolver-feature family: the namespace a `ResolverFeature:*` key is minted under. Every non-structural producer mints through `key`. The structural producer mints through `StructuralFeature::tag`, whose literals carry the same `structural:` prefix, so `from_feature_key` decodes it while the compiler does not enforce it there.

game::coverage::SemanticFinding.name: SemanticFinding
game::coverage::SemanticFinding.doc: A semantic finding detected during audit of a card's parsed data vs Oracle text.

variants.name: WrongAbilityType
variants.doc: Ability type mismatch: Oracle text suggests trigger but parsed as static, etc.

variants.name: UnimplementedSubEffect
variants.doc: A parsed ability contains Effect::Unimplemented or AbilityCost::Unimplemented sub-stubs.

variants.name: DroppedCondition
variants.doc: Condition field is None when Oracle text contains condition language.

variants.name: DroppedDuration
variants.doc: Duration field is None when Oracle text contains duration language.

variants.name: WrongParameter
variants.doc: Parsed numeric parameter doesn't match Oracle text.

variants.name: SilentDrop
variants.doc: Oracle line has no corresponding parsed item (silent drop).

game::deck_validation::SignatureSpellSel.name: SignatureSpellSelectionPolicy
game::deck_validation::SignatureSpellSel.doc: Engine-authored deck-builder state for selecting an Oathbreaker's signature spell. The frontend renders this policy but never derives the candidate list.

game::derived_views::CounterMagnitude.name: CounterMagnitude
game::derived_views::CounterMagnitude.doc: CR 122.1 + CR 732.2a: whether a counter row's count is a real quantity or one an accepted shortcut pumps without bound. Typed rather than a bool because the row is engine-classified data, not a render-time guess. `Finite` is the dominant case and is therefore the serde default, so the wire stays quiet for it.

game::derived_views::FamilyCollapseState.name: FamilyCollapseState
game::derived_views::FamilyCollapseState.doc: This family's collapse coverage. `Scheduled` displays `GameState::pending_unbounded_materialization` — growth whose count was fixed at accept and which is in flight along CR 732.2c's advance to the proposal's ending point, that point being a priority window per CR 732.2a and not the CR 500.5 boundary the stash is cashed out at (`types/game_state.rs`'s `scheduled_collapse_axes` doc, and this file's `THE WINDOW'S TIMING IS CR 732.2c'S ADVANCE` block). An earlier version of this doc called that stash unlicensed; it is not — see `scheduled_collapse_axes` for the four-position reading. `Mixed` is a join result.  `Unscheduled` is the one variant a CR describes, and only in the SHAPED sense the rest of this crate uses (this file's `IS AN ENGINE-STATE ARGUMENT, NOT A RULES ONE` block): CR 732.1b's antecedent is a state "in which a set of actions could be repeated indefinitely", and an ∞ axis with nothing staged is exactly that — a legal, ordinary game state, pre-proposal. The rule's PERMISSION clause is not what is cited and is never authority for engine conduct.  NOTE — distinct from `types/game_state.rs`'s `LoopCollapseAxis::Mixed`, which means "the stash spans ≥2 axis KINDS" and only labels the finite-count prompt.

game::derived_views::LegendCandidateIden.name: LegendCandidateIdentity
game::derived_views::LegendCandidateIden.doc: Engine-authored identity for a candidate in a legend-rule choice.  The frontend renders this value without inspecting token, copy-effect, or face-down state. `TokenCopy` takes precedence when a copied permanent spell resolved as a token; `Copy` is a live Layer 1a copy effect; `Original` is every other face-up candidate; `Unknown` withholds affirmative identity for a face-down candidate.

game::derived_views::PlayerConditionKind.name: PlayerConditionKind
game::derived_views::PlayerConditionKind.doc: A single player-affecting condition the HUD surfaces as a status icon.  **Presentation-only discriminant.** `kind` selects an icon + i18n key; it deliberately spans multiple CR sections (CR 104.2b, CR 119.7/.8, CR 118.3, CR 101.2 / CR 702.50b) because the display layer groups "conditions afflicting a player" regardless of which rules section produced them. The categorical-boundary rule governs *rules-primitive* enums; this lives in the `DerivedViews` presentation layer alongside `StackPaidFactView`, so the cross-section span is correct here, not a sibling-cluster smell. The authoritative rules state remains in `StaticMode`, `GameRestriction`, and `EpicEffect` — this enum never feeds game logic, only rendering.

variants.name: CantWin
variants.doc: CR 104.2b: effect-based win attempts targeting this player are no-ops.

variants.name: CantGainLife
variants.doc: CR 119.7: life-gain events affecting this player are replaced with nothing.

variants.name: CantLoseLife
variants.doc: CR 119.8: life-loss events affecting this player are replaced with nothing.

variants.name: CantPayLifeAsCost
variants.doc: CR 118.3: this player can't pay life as a cost.

variants.name: CantCastSpells
variants.doc: CR 101.2 / CR 702.50b: this player can't cast spells (Epic lock or a temporary `ProhibitActivity::CastSpells`, possibly spell-filtered — the `source` card identifies the specifics for the tooltip).

variants.name: CantActivateAbilities
variants.doc: CR 101.2 + CR 602.5: this player can't activate abilities (mana abilities may still be exempt — the `source` card identifies the specifics).

variants.name: CastOnlyFromZones
variants.doc: CR 101.2 + CR 601.2a: this player may cast spells only from the listed zones.

game::derived_views::TargetChoiceKind.name: TargetChoiceKind
game::derived_views::TargetChoiceKind.doc: CR 115.1: "The targets are object(s) and/or player(s) the spell or ability will affect." What the live target announcement is asking the announcing player to choose from, classified over that exact and/or axis — so a mixed offer is a representable value rather than a case that falls through.

variants.name: Players
variants.doc: CR 102.1: every offered choice is a player.

variants.name: Objects
variants.doc: CR 109.1: every offered choice is an object, of `category`.

variants.name: ObjectsAndPlayers
variants.doc: CR 115.1 + CR 115.4: the offer mixes objects of `category` with players — the "any target" shape.

game::derived_views::TargetObjectCategor.name: TargetObjectCategory
game::derived_views::TargetObjectCategor.doc: CR 109.1 + CR 205.2a: the narrowest category of the CR object taxonomy that is true of EVERY object in one announcement's offered choice set.

variants.name: Spell
variants.doc: CR 112.1: a spell — a card on the stack.

variants.name: Creature
variants.doc: CR 110.4: creature is one of the six permanent types.

variants.name: Planeswalker
variants.doc: CR 110.4: planeswalker is one of the six permanent types.

variants.name: NonlandPermanent
variants.doc: CR 110.4: permanents, none of which is a land.

variants.name: Permanent
variants.doc: CR 110.1: a permanent, with no narrower category true of all of them.

variants.name: Object
variants.doc: CR 109.1 + CR 115.2: an object with no narrower true category — a card in a graveyard/exile/library/hand, an ability on the stack (CR 113.7a), a mixed-zone offer, or an object this projection cannot resolve.

game::derived_views::UnboundedFamily.name: UnboundedFamily
game::derived_views::UnboundedFamily.doc: The display family an unbounded [`ResourceAxis`] groups into. No CR governs a display grouping (cf. `game/filter.rs`'s `context_free_prop_matches_face` Kleene `AnyOf` arm).  NOT `analysis::corpus::ResourceFamily` — different module, lossy family→representative-axis map, no total inverse, no `Poison`→counters variant.  `rename_all` so the wire strings ARE the client's family literals — one type, no mirror map. Pinned against the client's `Record<ResourceAxisTag, UnboundedFamily>` by the `unbounded-family-tags.json` golden, which carries all 17 axis-tag→family pairs.

game::dungeon::DungeonId.name: DungeonId
game::dungeon::DungeonId.doc: CR 309: The five dungeon cards across D&D crossover sets.

game::dungeon::VentureSource.name: VentureSource
game::dungeon::VentureSource.doc: Distinguishes normal venture from initiative-sourced venture. Typed enum per CLAUDE.md: "never a raw bool."

variants.name: Normal
variants.doc: CR 701.49a: Normal "venture into the dungeon" — offers AFR trio (Lost Mine, Tomb, Mad Mage). Also used for 701.49c re-entry.

variants.name: Specific
variants.doc: CR 701.49d: "venture into [quality]" — constrained to a specific dungeon. Currently only Undercity (via initiative), but general per CR 701.49d.

game::effects::choose_from_zone::PerPlay.name: PerPlayerDepartureRefusal
game::effects::choose_from_zone::PerPlay.doc: Why departure reconciliation could not proceed. The frame stays parked.

game::effects::counters::CounterAddition.name: CounterAdditionPreview
game::effects::counters::CounterAddition.doc: The replacement-aware result of previewing a counter addition.  This is intentionally an engine-internal decision fact rather than wire state: callers use it while evaluating a currently-bound action, so it must not be serialized or retained across object-incarnation changes.

variants.name: Applied
variants.doc: The proposed count reaches the object unchanged.

variants.name: Prevented
variants.doc: A replacement effect prevents the counter addition.

variants.name: ChoiceRequired
variants.doc: Replacement ordering or an optional replacement needs this player's choice.

variants.name: Transformed
variants.doc: Replacement effects change the proposed counter count.

variants.name: Unsupported
variants.doc: A replacement rewrites the counter event into a different event class.  The tactical preview cannot claim that the requested counter was added, so consumers must handle this explicitly rather than treating it as an absent preview.

game::effects::draw::DrawDeliveryPreview.name: DrawDeliveryPreview
game::effects::draw::DrawDeliveryPreview.doc: Exact delivery fact for one fully specified draw instruction.  This is deliberately a tactical, engine-internal result rather than state carried over the wire: library contents, draw restrictions, replacement candidates, and any continuation choice are all facts of the supplied state.

variants.name: Exact
variants.doc: The cloned instruction retired normally and its draw-sequence frame recorded this many actual Library-to-Hand deliveries.

variants.name: Unknown
variants.doc: The instruction parked at a player-owned decision, including a choice raised by a mandatory replacement's continuation.

game::effects::life::LifeAssignmentOutco.name: LifeAssignmentOutcome
game::effects::life::LifeAssignmentOutco.doc: Outcome of applying a life-total permutation via `apply_life_totals_assignment`.  Typed (not a bare bool) so the control-flow signal is self-documenting at call sites: `Applied` means the caller should emit its `EffectResolved`; `Deferred` means a competing replacement (CR 616.1) installed a choice `WaitingFor` and the caller must return without emitting — the resume path completes resolution.

game::effects::life::ReplacementDeferred.name: ReplacementDeferred
game::effects::life::ReplacementDeferred.doc: Why a replacement-routed life change could not complete synchronously.  Typed so phase-transition owners can distinguish the replacement-ordering round trip from a substitute effect that has already begun resolving and paused on its own interactive continuation.

variants.name: ReplacementChoice
variants.doc: CR 616.1: paused on the ordering choice BEFORE anything was applied. The pipeline reports the real amount when the choice resumes.

variants.name: SubstitutionContinuation
variants.doc: CR 614.6: the root event already finished for `applied`; what paused is the substitute effect that must resolve before the original resolution may continue.  Carrying the amount is load-bearing, not decorative: a caller that needs to narrate WHY the life changed (the empty-pool drain's mana burn) learns the true figure here and nowhere else. Dropping it forced that caller to park provenance and hope a later resume would hand the number back — and the resume that completes a substitute is not the one that applied the root, so the number never came.

game::effects::player_counter::PlayerCou.name: PlayerCounterAdditionOutcome
game::effects::player_counter::PlayerCou.doc: The replacement-aware outcome of attempting to add player counters.  Distinguished from a plain `bool` because callers fall into two families that need `Prevented` handled differently: - Effect resolution (`resolve` below, `deal_damage`'s infect/toxic poison,   `proliferate`, the pending-counter-addition drain in `counters.rs`)   treats `Applied` and `Prevented` identically — the pending item is fully   resolved either way, whether or not any counters actually landed. - Cost payment (`costs.rs`'s `GetPlayerCounters` ability-cost arm) must   treat `Prevented` as a FAILED payment: a "players can't get counters"   replacement (Solemnity) silently zeroing out a Ward's player-counter   cost must not be mistaken for having actually paid it, or Ward's whole   deterrent is bypassed for free (CR 702.21a).

variants.name: Applied
variants.doc: The counters were added (possibly replacement-adjusted in count).

variants.name: Prevented
variants.doc: A replacement effect prevented the counter addition outright.

variants.name: NeedsChoice
variants.doc: Replacement ordering or an optional replacement needs this player's choice; `state.waiting_for` has already been set.

game::effects::player_counter::PlayerCou.name: PlayerCounterAdditionPreview
game::effects::player_counter::PlayerCou.doc: The replacement-aware result of previewing a player-counter addition.  Mirrors `counters::CounterAdditionPreview` (the object-counter sibling), parameterized for players instead of an object incarnation — players have no incarnation-staleness concept, so there is no `None` "target no longer matches" case here.  This is intentionally an engine-internal decision fact rather than wire state: callers use it while evaluating a currently-bound action, so it must not be serialized or retained across turns.

variants.name: Applied
variants.doc: The proposed count reaches the player unchanged.

variants.name: Prevented
variants.doc: A replacement effect prevents the counter addition.

variants.name: ChoiceRequired
variants.doc: Replacement ordering or an optional replacement needs this player's choice.

variants.name: Transformed
variants.doc: Replacement effects change the proposed counter count (e.g. a doubler).

variants.name: Unsupported
variants.doc: A replacement rewrites the counter event into a different event class.  The preview cannot claim that the requested counter was added, so consumers must handle this explicitly rather than treating it as an absent preview.

game::engine::BoundedOfferRefusal.name: BoundedOfferRefusal
game::engine::BoundedOfferRefusal.doc: CR 732.2a: which conjunct of [`try_offer_bounded_cycle_shortcut`] refused to offer.  Exhaustive and typed, in the order the conjuncts run. Production ignores the value (a refusal is a refusal), but a negative test row must be able to say WHICH conjunct it is about: an assertion that merely observes "no offer" silently stops testing its own conjunct the moment an earlier one starts refusing first.

variants.name: NotAtPriority
variants.doc: (1) Not a `WaitingFor::Priority` beat, so nobody may suggest a shortcut.

variants.name: ProposerIsNotActivePlayer
variants.doc: (2) The priority holder is not the active player the ring sampler gates on.

variants.name: NoCertification
variants.doc: (4) Neither certification basis matched.

variants.name: AdvantageOnlyCycle
variants.doc: (5) `WinKind::Advantage` — no CR 704 threshold, so this is Path C's class.

variants.name: UnspecifiedChoiceWindow
variants.doc: (6) A per-iteration choice the cycle opens is not specified by a published slot.

variants.name: NoNarrowedLegalCount
variants.doc: (7) `elimination_cascade` measured no CR 704 threshold at all and no cleanup bound, or measured one under which no repetition is legal. Both grounds refuse here, because both leave this producer with nothing to state: its whole claim is a threshold it measured inside the loop.

variants.name: ActivationReversed
variants.doc: CR 601.2h + CR 733.1: the in-progress activation of `player` can't be completed legally (its locked total is unpayable), so the whole activation is reversed.
